review_notes:
I read all of SignCaps.lean (four lemmas, lines 6–28). I also read the lemmas they use: exact_table_error in DerivativeEnvelope.lean, the perturbation_*_cap lemmas in SignBounds.lean, and the *_le_rat and *_le_half lemmas in RationalBounds.lean. I checked the downstream uses in OriginPositive, HalfGapTypes and HalfGapSmall.

The four proofs do follow one pattern. Each applies exact_table_error, then uses add_le_add and mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left to bound 3/10^5*(directEnvelope+transformEnvelope) by the rational cap, then closes with a perturbation_*_cap lemma. Two of them wrap the chain in div_le_div_of_nonneg_right for the /2.

The repeated part is only a monotonicity chain over existing API. A shared helper would take hypotheses directEnvelope ell ≤ D and transformEnvelope ell s ≤ T and conclude |…| ≤ 3/10^5*(D+T). It would be a thin wrapper around add_le_add and mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left, and it would save about one line per use. That is routine unfolding of the kind the rubric calls insufficient, so I am not reporting a finding.

The real numerical work sits in the separate norm_num lemmas, which are different for each case. The remaining uncertainty is whether a helper that also absorbed the /2 and trans_lt steps would be worthwhile. I judged it marginal.
